title: Repeat offender fined for searching for gold in protected river
summary: Brian Wright, 68, from Henley-upon-Thames, was caught gold panning on a protected river in north Wales.
text: Repeat offender gold panner caught in protected Afon Wen river - BBC News BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu BBC News Menu Home Climate World US & Canada UK Business Tech Science Entertainment & Arts Health More In Pictures BBC Verify Newsbeat Wales Wales Politics Wales Business North West North East Mid South West South East Cymru Local News Repeat offender fined for searching for gold in protected river Image source, David Powell / North Wales Daily Post Image caption, Brian Wright was caught panning at Afon Wen river near Dolgellau, Gwynedd By Paul Pigott BBC Wales Published 17 September 2026 A gold panner caught illegally searching for gold in a protected river has been ordered to pay fines and costs totalling more than £4,700, a regulator has said. Brian Wright, 68, had been caught panning at Afon Wen river near Dolgellau, Gwynedd, in October and December 2024. He was found guilty of environmental offences at Llandudno Magistrate's Court on Monday. Environment body Natural Resources Wales (NRW) said Wright had been caught disturbing the "protected and valued environment" of Coed y Brenin Forest, which the river runs through, and was a repeat offender. "Activities such as illegal gold panning can cause significant damage to river habitats and wildlife," said NRW's Richard Berry. "This case should serve as a reminder that illegal gold panning is not permitted on NRW-managed land and those who ignore the rules may face prosecution." The environment body said the excavation of gravel and the removal of minerals could disturb riverbeds, impacting habitats that wildlife rely on. It said that although many were unaware of the repercussions, gold panning could lead to prosecution and sentencing "where it risks disturbing spawning fish and impacting river habitats". It also said Wright, from Henley On Thames, Oxfordshire, had been sentenced for similar offences in May 2022. NRW manager for north-west Wales, Euros Jones, told BBC Radio Wales Breakfast that gold panning was "damaging" and could lead to a "concerning environmental cost". Jones said Dolgellau "has a history of gold mining" and very small specks of gold could be found among "a lot of gravel". "There is a romance around the gold, and it does attract people to the river because it is known for this," he said.
